context: Tests whether the agent reaches for the event handler feature for human-readable per-step output — the right tool for development/demo surface — rather than reaching for OpenTelemetry (production signal, overkill here) or hand-rolling println scaffolding inside tool bodies.

checklist.name: Installs the event-handler feature
checklist.description: Calls handleEvents { ... } inside the AIAgent(...) trailing lambda. Does NOT install OpenTelemetry (overkill for stdout demo output and adds collector setup) and does NOT add println calls inside each tool body

checklist.name: Adds the agents-features-event-handler dependency
checklist.description: Adds ai.koog:agents-features-event-handler to build.gradle.kts at 1.3.0 with each artifact on its stable or beta line. The umbrella does not include the event handler

checklist.name: Subscribes to onToolCallStarting
checklist.description: Registers an onToolCallStarting handler that prints tool name and arguments. The start-side callback is essential for the live demo trace

checklist.name: Subscribes to onToolCallFinished
checklist.description: Registers an onToolCallFinished handler that prints the tool result (or at minimum a completion marker). The task requires surfacing when each tool completes — both start and finish callbacks are needed

checklist.name: Uses distinct visual markers for start vs end
checklist.description: Uses visually distinct prefixes between start and end output (e.g., → vs ←, or [start] vs [end]) so the audience can read the trace at scroll speed

checklist.name: Does not also install OpenTelemetry
checklist.description: Does not add OpenTelemetry on top — the developer explicitly said no Langfuse/OTel for this demo. Adding it would require collector setup and isn't requested
